note: Declarative list of what macro.py fetches. Each series: id, source (adapter), source_id, name and one-line 'what', unit, freq (D/W/M/Q/A), kind (index: % changes; count: level changes; rate: percentage-point changes; flow: monthly flows summed over 12 months), release, group, store (false = third-party copyright: never fetched into this public repo), priority, licence, revised, stale_after_days (backstop when the release calendar does not cover the series). Views carry their fixed thresholds here so a reader can see them.

trend_rule: Trend leg (the board's one definition, regime_core / regime.py): +1 when the series is above a rising 50-session exponential average (rising = higher than 21 sessions earlier), -1 when below a falling one, 0 otherwise.

side_rule.text: Each test sits WITH the view when its value is beyond the 'confirm' threshold, AGAINST it when beyond the 'refute' threshold, and NEITHER in between. With c tests with and r against: c - r >= 2 is 'with'; c - r = 1 is 'leaning with'; c = r (both above zero) is 'mixed'; no test past either threshold is 'neutral'; r - c = 1 is 'leaning against'; r - c >= 2 is 'against'. Fewer than half the tests with data is 'not enough data'.

codes.with: The data sit with this view
codes.lean_with: The data lean toward this view
codes.mixed: The data are split on this view
codes.neutral: The data sit between the thresholds on this view
codes.lean_against: The data lean against this view
codes.against: The data sit against this view
codes.insufficient: Not enough data to place this view

reads.title: Labour-market temperature
reads.formula: Mean of five robust z-scores, each against its own trailing 10 years (median and 1.4826 x median absolute deviation, so 2020 does not swamp the scale), signed so positive means tighter: minus the 3-month change in the unemployment rate; minus initial claims' 4-week average against its own 52-week average (%); the 3-month average payroll change; the quits rate; job openings per unemployed person. Shown with the Sahm gap: 3-month average unemployment rate minus its lowest 3-month average of the prior 12 months.
reads.limits: The October 2025 household-survey gap blanks 3-month averages that span it. The payroll pace that keeps unemployment steady is uncertain while immigration shifts labour supply, so payroll change is read against its own history, not a fixed neutral number. The Sahm gap's 0.5 pp line marked the start of every US recession since 1970 and triggered in August 2024 without one.

reads.title: Wages against productivity and prices
reads.formula: Employment Cost Index wages, year over year, minus labour productivity, year over year (4-quarter changes); compared with core PCE prices, year over year.
reads.limits: Arithmetic identity (wage growth minus productivity growth is unit-labour-cost growth); no track record claimed. Productivity is noisy quarter to quarter.

reads.title: Breadth of inflation
reads.formula: Three gaps: median CPI minus headline CPI, and trimmed-mean CPI minus headline CPI (each the 3-month average of the monthly annual rate against headline's 3-month annualised change); sticky-price core minus flexible-price CPI, year over year.
reads.limits: The share of the ~70 CPI categories rising faster than 3% needs the BLS key (not created yet), so only the three gaps are shown.

reads.title: Fed reaction: policy rate, rule and market path
reads.formula: Policy-range midpoint; the Atlanta Fed Taylor-rule utility's FOMCTaylor99UR prescription; the fed funds futures strip's implied rate for the next policy month and about 6 and 12 months out (100 minus price); the latest FOMC median projections. Value: the change the futures price over about 12 months (pp).
reads.limits: The neutral rate inside any Taylor rule is disputed; the utility shows one documented choice. Futures embed a term premium, so they are not a pure expectation.

reads.title: Fiscal impulse
reads.formula: 12-month primary deficit (deficit excluding interest on the public debt) as a share of nominal GDP, now minus 12 months earlier, in percentage points; positive means fiscal policy is putting more into demand than a year ago. Tariff refunds are shown as a separate line.
reads.limits: Payment-timing shifts move single months, so only 12-month sums are used. A tariff refund is a one-off transfer to importers, not a policy stance. The Brookings Hutchins Fiscal Impact Measure is the published comparator (availability not established).

reads.title: Small against large businesses
reads.formula: Rows, each small minus large where a pair exists: banks tightening to small firms minus to large and mid firms (net %); business applications, year over year; trend of the small-cap to large-cap price ratio (IWM / SPY) and of small to mid (IJR / IJH), by the board's trend-leg rule.
reads.limits: ADP payrolls by firm size are third-party copyright and are not published here, so the payroll row is missing in v1.

reads.title: Dollar, emerging markets and Europe: the relative cycle
reads.formula: Broad dollar, year over year; BIS real effective dollar, year over year; 2-year Treasury yield minus the euro overnight rate (pp); OECD leading indicators for the US, Germany and China; trend legs for EEM / SPY, VGK / SPY, EMLC and CEW.
reads.limits: Leading indicators are revised heavily; compare levels across countries at one vintage. No track record claimed.

reads.title: Capital spending as an inflation input
reads.formula: 3-month annualised growth of data-centre construction, core capital-goods orders and transformer prices, beside electricity prices and construction wages, year over year.
reads.limits: Census construction data are revised in place with no vintages. No track record claimed.
